name: Abidan
overview: Abidan was a male leader from the tribe of Benjamin, serving as the head of his tribe during the census recorded in Numbers 1:11. He played a significant role as a leader of Benjamin during the Exodus, overseeing his tribe in this important period of Israel's journey. His leadership is specifically noted in the context of the census, indicating his responsibility and standing among the Israelites.
namesAndTitles: The name Abidan means '[my] father is judge,' reflecting a name of Hebrew origin. This proper name, given independently of divine naming, underscores a heritage or identity possibly connected to judgment or leadership, fitting for a tribal head.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Abidan was the father of Gideoni, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are noted, and no additional familial details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abidan's significance lies in his role as the appointed leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the critical period of the Exodus and the census of Israel. His leadership helped organize and represent his tribe within the larger community of Israel as they prepared to enter the Promised Land. By overseeing the census, Abidan contributed to the orderly arrangement and mobilization of the Israelite tribes under God's direction.
